svg.title: How a Slack message reaches your clone and its reply gets back
svg.desc: Inside your Mac, a message travels from your signed-in Slack tab to the extension service worker, the native host and the Misha app, which hands it to the clone turn. The app acknowledges it back to the service worker. The clone thinks with a model provider outside the Mac, reads the thread through the native host and your tab, reads your linked folders, and reads GitHub and your connected services. Its post goes back through the app, which holds it on Home for your OK while approvals are on, then through the native host, the service worker and the tab to Slack, which sends it back as an echo. On a turn that may start work, the clone starts one or more workers, held for your OK while approvals are on; each calls a model provider and your services and reports back to the app. Twelve numbered steps in the list under the diagram describe each arrow.
